name: HEX_PROCESS_METADATA
description: The table stores the metadata for the process being executed.

columns.name: PROCESS_ID
columns.description: The column indicates a sequence generated value.

columns.name: PROCESS_CODE
columns.description: The column indicates the Consumer Process Code.

columns.name: PROCESS_NAME
columns.description: The column indicates the Consumer Process Name.

columns.name: CLASS_NAME
columns.description: The column indicates the Consumer Implementation Class Name.

columns.name: SUB_CLASS_NAME
columns.description: The column indicates the Consumer Implementation Sub Class Name.

columns.name: PRE_PROCESS_PROCEDURE
columns.description: The column indicates the Consumer Implementation pre process Procedure Name.

columns.name: PROCESS_PROCEDURE
columns.description: The column indicates the Consumer Implementation Procedure Name.

columns.name: POST_PROCESS_PROCEDURE
columns.description: The column indicates the Consumer Implementation post process Procedure Name.

columns.name: ACTIVE_STATUS
columns.description: The column indicates if the specified process is active.

columns.name: DEFAULT_THREADS
columns.description: The column indicates the Default Thread Count value.

columns.name: DEFAULT_CHUNK_SIZE
columns.description: The column indicates the Default Chunk Size value.

columns.name: DEFAULT_LOGGING
columns.description: The column indicates the Default Logging value.

columns.name: DEFAULT_MAX_ERRORS
columns.description: The column indicates the Default Max Errors Allowed value.

columns.name: ALLOW_OVERRIDE_DEFAULTS
columns.description: The column indicates if the default values can be overridden with Payroll Configuration Group.

columns.name: CONFIG_GROUP_TYPE
columns.description: The column indicates the type of configuration group used.

columns.name: DEFAULT_CONFIG_GROUP
columns.description: The column indicates the default configuration group to be used for the process.

columns.name: RETRIES
columns.description: The column indicates the number of retries allowed.

columns.name: ELEVATED
columns.description: The column indicates if the current process is elevated. Valid values are Y and N.Default value is N.

columns.name: MODULE_ID
columns.description: Seed Data Framework: indicates the module that owns the row. A module is an entry in Application Taxonomy such as a Logical Business Area. When the MODULE_ID column exists and the owner of the row is not specified, then the Seed Data Framework will not extract the row as seed data.

columns.name: ENTERPRISE_ID
columns.description: Identifier of Enterprise, used for multi-tenancy partitioning. Foreign key to HR_ORGANIZATION_UNITS.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.description: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.name: CREATED_BY
columns.description: Who column: indicates the user who created the row.

columns.name: CREATION_DATE
columns.description: Who column: indicates the date and time of the creation of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATED_BY
columns.description: Who column: indicates the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_DATE
columns.description: Who column: indicates the date and time of the last update of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_LOGIN
columns.description: Who column: indicates the session login associated to the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: SGUID
columns.description: The seed global unique identifier. Oracle internal use only.

columns.name: SEED_DATA_SOURCE
columns.description: Source of seed data record. A value of 'BULK_SEED_DATA_SCRIPT' indicates that record was bulk loaded. Otherwise, specifies the name of the seed data file.

columns.name: ORA_SEED_SET1
columns.description: Oracle internal use only. Indicates the edition-based redefinition (EBR) context of the row for SET1. Context values are Y or N.

columns.name: ORA_SEED_SET2
columns.description: Oracle internal use only. Indicates the edition-based redefinition (EBR) context of the row for SET2. Context values are Y or N.
